sentences.text:
Briefly stated the facts as per record are as under:-
An FIR No. 443/2021 was lodged at PS Ambedkar Nagar on 07.07.2021 for the offences u/s 498A/406/34 IPC.
Said FIR was registered on the basis of complaint dated 11.11.2020 given by Smt. Barkha (respondent herein).
As per the contents of the FIR, Barkha (respondent herein) got married to Sumit s/o Late Sh. Suresh Verma on 08.03.2019.
After 2-3 days of the marriage, her mother in law and sisters in law namely Smt. Prem Lata, Ms. Shikha and Ms. Sandhya started quarreling with her and started beating her.
It is alleged that husband of the complainant/respondent after consuming liquor used to beat her and kicked her out of the house at night.
Complainant/respondent further alleged that her husband Sumit along with his maternal uncle namely Lekhchand @ Bablu Barafwala and her mother-in- law Prem Lata used to abuse her, beat her.
After 3 months of marriage the jewellery articles of the complainant were kept by the husband and mother in law of the complainant against her wishes and she was turned out of the house.
On the request of the complainant she was again taken back to the house by her husband.
It is further alleged that the husband and mother-in-law of the complainant/respondent used to harass her as she gave birth to a female child against their wishes as they expected a male child.
Allegedly, they did not even visit hospital to see the girl and demanded Rs. 5,00,000/- as a condition to take her back to their house.
It is further alleged that the husband and the mother in law casted aspersions on her character and even refused to accept the girl child alleging her to be of someone else.
Accordingly, FIR was registered.
3. On this basis, FIR was registered and the investigation was carried out.

During investigation,
testimonies of witnesses were recorded and on the basis of the same, charge-sheet was filed for the offences u/s 498A/406/34 IPC against the revisionists before Ld. Trial Court on 16.04.2022.
Cognizance for said offences was taken on 16.04.2022.

Arguments were heard on the point of charge and after considering the same alongwith material on record, the charge was ordered to be framed against Sumit, Premlata, Lekhchand @ Barafwala @ Babu, Shikha and Sandhya for the offences u/s 498A IPC and against Sumit and Premlata u/s 406 IPC vide detailed order dated 13.07.2023 of Ld.
Metropolitan Magistrate-4 (Mahila Court), South District, Saket.

entities.text: Metropolitan Magistrate-4 (Mahila Court), South District, Saket
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Formal charge in pursuance to that order was framed on 16.08.2023.

The order on charge dated 13.07.2023 and framing of charge on 16.08.2023 are being challenged in the present revision petition by the revisionists namely Premlata, Lekhchand @ Barafwala @ Babu, Shikha and Sandhya.
4. It has been argued by Ld. Counsel for revisionists that the allegations made by the complainant in her statement u/s 161 Cr.P.C. are completely false.
It is further argued that there are no specific allegations against the revisionist that can attract the offences for which charge has been framed.
Even the name of the sisters in law are not mentioned in the allegations made by the complainant.

It is further argued that there is no independent witness or the medical evidence on record to corroborate the version of the complainant and only vague allegations without any particulars have been made against the revisionist.
Ld. Counsel further argued that the Ld. Trial court has not appreciated the facts properly and erroneously framed the charge against the revisionist.

Premlata vs Barkha on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181527163/
2 5.

entities.text: Premlata vs Barkha on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, Ld. Addl.PP for State has submitted that there is no illegality in the framing of charge against the revisionists as there is sufficient material on record to justify the same.
It was also argued that at the stage of framing of charge, the Trial Court has to see only the prima facie material on record and same has been done in the present matter so there is no illegality.

Further it is submitted that the contentions raised by the Ld. Counsel for the revisionist can only be dealt after adducing the evidence and on conclusion of the trial but as of now there is sufficient material to proceed against the revisionist in this case.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of the revision petition.
6. I have considered the submissions from both the sides alongwith record.
7. It is settled law that at the stage of framing of charge, Trial Court is to see as to whether a prima facie case is made out against the accused after considering the material on record.

Hon'ble Apex Court in Onkar Nath Mishra and Ors. Vs. State ( NCT of Delhi) and Anr. (2008) 2 SCC 561 held as under:-
"11.

entities.text: Onkar Nath Mishra and Ors. Vs. State ( NCT of Delhi) and Anr. (2008) 2 SCC 561
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is trite that at the stage of framing of charge the Court is required to evaluate the material and documents on record with a view to finding out if the facts emerging therefrom, taken at their face value, disclosed the existence of all the ingredients constituting the alleged offence.
At that stage, the Court is not expected to go deep into the probative value of the material on record.
What needs to be considered is whether there is a ground for presuming that the offence has been committed and not a ground for convicting the accused has been made out.

At this stage, even strong suspicion founded on material which leads the Court to form a presumptive opinion as to existence of the factual ingredients constituting the offence alleged would justify the framing of charge against the accused in respect of the commission of that offence."

8. Similar observations were made by Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of Maharashtra & Ors. Vs.
Som Nath Thapa and Ors. 1996 Cri.LJ 2448 in following words:-
"If on the basis of materials on record, a court could come to the conclusion that commission of the offence is a probable consequence, a case for framing of charge exists.

entities.text:
State of Maharashtra & Ors. Vs.
Som Nath Thapa and Ors. 1996 Cri.LJ 2448
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To put it differently, if the Court were to think that the accused might have committed the offence it can frame the charge, though for conviction the conclusion is required to be that the accused has committed the offence.

It is apparent that at the stage of framing of charge, probative value of the materials on record cannot be gone into; the materials brought on record by the prosecution has to be accepted as true at that stage."

9. The Ld. Trial Court in the impugned order dated 13.07.2023 has elaborately dealt with the contentions raised before this court and reached at the conclusion that the arguments raised by Ld.
Counsel from the revisionists relating to vagueness and contradiction in the allegations are primarily in the nature of defence to be established during the course of trial.

While reaching at the Premlata vs Barkha on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181527163/
3 conclusion that there was sufficient material on record to proceed against the revisionist, Ld.

entities.text: Premlata vs Barkha on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Trial court placed reliance upon the judgment passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case titled as State of Maharashtra v. Priyasharan Maharaj and others in criminal appeal no. 263/1997.

entities.text: State of Maharashtra v. Priyasharan Maharaj and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It was observed by the Hon'ble Apex court that "at the stage of framing of charge, the court has to consider the material with a view to find out if there is ground for presuming that the accused has committed the offence or that there is no sufficient ground for proceeding against him and not for the purpose of arriving at conclusion that it is not likely to lead to a conviction".
10.

The Ld. Trial Court observed in the impugned order that there are specific allegations against the revisionists Prem Lata, Lekh Chand, Shikha and Sandhya and therefore prima facie commission of offences as charged were framed by the Ld. Trial Court.
This court has gone through the trial court record and the statements of the witnesses recorded therein.
It can be seen that the complainant has specifically named the revisionist Lekhchand @ Barfwala @ Bablu who harassed her and even threatened her to remove the complainant from the matrimonial house.
It is also seen from the statement of the complainant as well as her mother Babli that there are specific allegations of cruelty being caused by revisionist Prem Lata, Shikha and Sandhya.
Even the nature of their act by which they harassed the complainant is also specified.
Now, whether the allegations are true or false are matter of trial.

However, considering the record, this Court is of the view that there was sufficient material on record to frame the respective charge against the revisionists and charge has been rightly framed against them by the Ld. Trial Court.

The contentions raised by the Ld. Counsel for the revisionist are in the form of plea of defence that can only be established at the time of adducing evidence and by subjecting the witness to cross examination to elicit truth out of the same.

11. In Soma Chakravarty v. State (2007) 5 SCC 403, Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that:-
"10.

It may be mentioned that the settled legal position, as mentioned in the above decisions, is that if on the basis of material on record the court could form an opinion that the accused might have committed the offence it can frame the charge, though for conviction the conclusion is required to be proved beyond reasonable doubt that the accused has committed the offence at the time of framing of the charges the probative value of the material on record cannot be gone into, and the material brought on record by the prosecution has to be accepted as true at that stage.
Before framing a charge the Court must apply its judicial mind on the material placed on record and must be satisfied that the commitment of offence by the accused was possible.
Whether, in fact, the accused committed the offence, can only be decided in the trial".

12. Therefore, in view of the discussion above and the settled position of law laid down by the aforesaid judgment with respect to the framing of charge, this court is of the view that the Ld. Trial Court has not committed any error in passing the impugned order dated 13.07.2023 and the order of charge is passed within the ambit of law.
13. It is settled position of law that while exercising the power of revisional jurisdiction, this Court can interefere only when the impugned order is perverse or untenable in law.

Reliance is placed Premlata vs Barkha on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181527163/
4 upon judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Sanjaysinh Ramrao Chavan vs. Dattatray Gulabrao Phalke and others, 2015 (3) SCC 123 wherein it has been observed as under :

entities.text: Sanjaysinh Ramrao Chavan vs. Dattatray Gulabrao Phalke and others, 2015 (3) SCC 123
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "14 .....Unless the order passed by the Magistrate is perverse or the view taken by the court is wholly unreasonable or there is non-consideration of any relevant material or there is palpable misreading of records, the Revisional Court is not justified in setting aside the order, merely because another view is possible.
The Revisional Court is not meant to act as an appellate court.
The whole purpose of the revisional jurisdiction is to preserve the power in the court to do justice in accordance with the principles of criminal jurisprudence.
The revisional power of the court under Sections 397 to 401 CrPC is not to be equated with that of an appeal.

Unless the finding of the court, whose decision is sought to be revised, is shown to be perverse or untenable in law or is grossly erroneous or glaringly unreasonable or where the decision is based on no material or where the material facts are wholly ignored or where the judicial discretion is exercised arbitrarily or capriciously, the courts may not interfere with decision in exercise of their revisional jurisdiction."
14. In the above case also conviction of the accused was recorded, the High Court set aside the order of conviction by substituting its own view.

This Court set aside the High Court's order holding that the High Court exceeded its jurisdiction in substituting its views and that too without any legal basis."
14.

Considering the above, this Court is of the view that Ld. Magistrate has passed the impugned order after considering all the relevant factors and there is no illegality so as to justify interference by this Court in revisional jurisdiction.
Accordingly, the revision petition stands dismissed.
15. Trial court record be sent back along with copy of the order.
16. The present revision be consigned to record room.
